text:
Josh Morrissey scored his first goal of the season in overtime to beat the Islanders last week, and the Jets' comeback that night was the kind of game that keeps a season afloat. He has played ten games, at 24 minutes a night, with seven points.

Underneath it, our numbers are more cautious. Winnipeg takes 47% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on (expected goals measure the quality of chances), about the same as without him, and the team has scored nearly 10 more goals than its chances with him on the ice. That kind of luck does not last, and some of his points will fade with it. Evolving-Hockey had him 17th among 215 defensemen last season, mostly from even-strength offense, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking still shows a clean puck mover, 61% of exits with possession. In the first season without Connor Hellebuyck behind him, Morrissey's defensive minutes matter more than they used to.
